notes: Worst-case Whisper-style transcript of a three-person startup weekly meeting (S1 founder, S2 CTO, S3 customer success) in Taiwanese Mandarin: practically no punctuation (spaces only), English terms inside Mandarin (sprint, ticket, backlog, P0, QA, MRR, burn rate, runway, churn, term sheet, pre-money, onboarding), Taiwanese particles (啦 喔 耶 欸 齁), numbers and dates in mixed formats (38萬, 4萬2, 3/11, 3月21號, 三月二十八號, 禮拜三, 百分之二點三 next to 1.8%, 一成六七 next to 14.3%, 1.2億, 2000萬), homophone slips (全限 for 權限, 稀式 for 稀釋, 對其 for 對齊, 穿接 for 串接, 平估 for 評估) and a company name that the ASR spells two ways (鯨落創投 and 京洛). A sentence is split across turn boundaries (the latency figure). Tests: (1) echoes of numbers and dates in the next speaker's turn, including S1's recap of S2's and S3's commitments (a point must carry only the speaker's own new claim); (2) vocatives by fictional nicknames (阿凱, 小安, 老大); (3) bare answers (7折, 沒問題, 對我記好了) that only make sense with the previous question; (4) pronouns whose referent sits in an earlier turn or is never named (他們 = a customer, a competitor or the investor, 他 = the hiring candidate, 她 = the shop owner); (5) quotes of absent third parties (customers and the investor); (6) one overlapped S0 turn with a date nobody may be credited with; (7) two speakers giving different dilution figures for the same deal (merge trap); (8) code-switched turns. Every key is unique to its speaker except the declared echoes.
